findings.specText: BalancerPoolerMintDebtHook NatSpec: 'Exclusive upper bound on `ratio`. Max settable ratio is `MAX_RATIO - 1`.' / '@param newRatio Must be strictly less than `MAX_RATIO` (50).' / field doc 'Strictly `< MAX_RATIO`'. story-030 body: 'ratio ... strictly capped below MAX_RATIO = 50'. UniboostMintDebtHook carries the identical NatSpec.
findings.specSource: src NatSpec (BalancerPoolerMintDebtHook.sol L23,L42,L76; UniboostMintDebtHook.sol L30,L55,L95) + git commit c94bf40 [story-030] body
findings.actualBehavior: setRatio guards with `if (newRatio > MAX_RATIO) revert RatioTooHigh();` which ACCEPTS newRatio == 50 (inclusive). Both hooks now seed DEFAULT_RATIO = 50, so the default value itself equals MAX_RATIO and could not exist under a strict-below-50 cap.
findings.deviation: NatSpec (and the original story-030 intent) says the cap is exclusive (max settable 49), but the code cap is inclusive (max settable 50). Conflicting sources. The later commit 924b188 ('raised ratio because sUSDS appreciation') changed DEFAULT_RATIO 30->50 without touching the guard or the NatSpec, so the *code* is faithful to the newest intent (default 50 requires an inclusive guard) and it is the NatSpec that is stale. Contrast the sibling NudgeRatchetMintDebtHook, whose story-035 deliberately made both guard AND NatSpec inclusive ('200 is accepted') — the two USDS/prime hooks were simply never doc-synced.
findings.authoritativeSource: code (per commit 924b188); the 'Exclusive / MAX_RATIO-1 / strictly <' NatSpec is stale documentation, not the intended behaviour
findings.securityOrValueImpact: none — ratio 50 vs 49 mints phUSD at 50% vs 49% of prime dispatched; both are far below 100%, so the protocol is heavily over-backed either way. Pure doc/code conformance.
findings.crossRef: profiles A6-ratio-boundary-natspec (surface-qa); prior-run L-09 lineage unrelated

findings.specText: story-043: 'Sibling of NudgeRatchet that HOLDS USDC on _dispatch (no transfer) ... onlyReleaser-gated release(amount) forwarding held USDC to batchMinter ... Mint-debt logic unchanged via the base hook.' In-source: 'Debt/release timing is DECOUPLED ON PURPOSE. phUSD mint-debt accrues (and the downstream staker may realise phUSD via the hook's pull()) at DISPATCH time, while the USDC backing it can still be sitting on this contract, un-released.'
findings.specSource: git commit f46a5cb [story-043] body + NudgeRatchetDelayRelease.sol L20-34 dev NatSpec
findings.actualBehavior: Implementation is FAITHFUL to the story: _dispatch is view/no-transfer (holds USDC), hook.onDispatch still accrues mint-debt against `amount` at dispatch time via the base, release(amount) is onlyReleaser+nonReentrant and safeTransfers held USDC to batchMinter. hookTypeId guard preserved.
findings.deviation: No conformance deviation. Recorded as a story-unsafe *review* item: the story's own intent creates an admin-controlled window where phUSD debt is realisable (hook.pull mints) before the backing USDC reaches batchMinter. Law-1 override was evaluated and does NOT fire: backing is HELD on this contract from dispatch onward and release only RELOCATES it, so total system backing is conserved; there is no unprivileged path to unbacked phUSD. The only way to break backing is trusted owner rescueERC20 pulling _token (see A4 footgun, Law-3).
findings.securityOrValueImpact: OOS under DEDUP-001 (phUSD unbacked-mint boundary is an external protocol-token trust assumption). Kept as a VISIBLE spec-conformance/manual-review record per Law-1 recall rule; not a security escalation because no unprivileged actor can violate the cross-contract backing invariant.
findings.crossRef: DEDUP-001 (unbacked phUSD mint authority); profiles A3-DEDUP-001-mint-authority, A4-ratchet-rescue-underbacking; prior-run L-12

findings.specText: Base pause semantics: ATokenDispatcherV2.dispatch is whenNotPaused; NudgeRatchetDelayRelease NatSpec 'rescueERC20 ... NOT pause-gated, by design.'
findings.actualBehavior: release() carries only onlyReleaser+nonReentrant and rescueERC20() only onlyOwner — neither has whenNotPaused. Pausing the dispatcher freezes NEW dispatch (inflow) but does NOT freeze custody: a releaser can still move held USDC to batchMinter and the owner can still rescue during a pause. Confirmed unchanged at f46a5cb.
findings.deviation: Prior-run L-12 restated for confirmation: pause does not freeze already-held custody. This is documented as intentional for rescueERC20 (escape hatch must work during pause). No NEW deviation; carryover Low footgun.
findings.securityOrValueImpact: Low operational footgun — a pause invoked to stop backing egress during an incident would not stop release(); trusted releaser/owner only.

faithfulConfirmations.claim: Scale 6-dp USDC up by 1e12 to 18-dp phUSD before applying ratio.
faithfulConfirmations.verdict: FAITHFUL — USDC_TO_PHUSD_SCALE = 1e12; added = (amount * 1e12 * ratio)/100, floored (never over-credits). Correct direction (M-03 lineage); no 1e30 sign/magnitude trap present.
faithfulConfirmations.correctByConstruction: NudgeRatchet ctor hard-guards token decimals()==6, so the fixed 1e12 scale matches the guaranteed prime decimals.

faithfulConfirmations.claim: hookTypeId marker guard so _dispatch asserts installed hook is genuinely NudgeRatchetMintDebtHook (Audit M-04).
faithfulConfirmations.verdict: FAITHFUL — both dispatchers require INudgeRatchetMintDebtHook(hook).hookTypeId() == keccak256('NudgeRatchetMintDebtHook.v1') in _dispatch; reverts on DefaultDispatchHook/wrong hook. Local EXPECTED_HOOK_TYPE_ID literal matches hook HOOK_TYPE_ID literal (drift-watch: 3 copies, all identical at f46a5cb).

faithfulConfirmations.claim: Sweep full USDC balance to batchMinter with bal >= amount defense-in-depth guard; amount reinterpreted as floor/mint-debt basis.
faithfulConfirmations.verdict: FAITHFUL — _dispatch reads full balance, require(bal >= amount), safeTransfer(batchMinter, bal). Surplus over amount = over-backing (safe direction). Matches story exactly.

faithfulConfirmations.claim: Buy-and-pool zap: _dispatch carves donationSplit% to recipient, retains rest; pool() swaps retained prime->pair, ~half pair->target, addLiquidity (LP as POL); debt hook prime-decimals-aware scale=10**(18-d).
faithfulConfirmations.verdict: FAITHFUL — _dispatch donation carve matches (donationEnabled = recipient!=0 && split>0, donationAmount = amount*split/100); base accrues debt on GROSS amount. pool() 3-step matches story. Hook ctor reads primeToken decimals, require d<=18, scale=10**(18-d). All conform.

faithfulConfirmations.claim: Uniboost.pool gains leading amountIn (4-arg) with amountIn>0 + amountIn<=balance checks; MultiPooler Ownable PoolCall[] batch, onlyPooler gate, atomic all-or-nothing forward.
faithfulConfirmations.verdict: FAITHFUL — Uniboost.pool(amountIn,minPairOut,minTargetOut,minLP) has require(amountIn>0) and require(amountIn<=balanceOf(this)); steps 2-3 + Pooled emit unchanged. MultiPooler forwards one IUniboostPooler.pool per row, onlyPooler, no try/catch => any revert bubbles (atomic). IUniboostPooler intentionally excludes BalancerPoolerV2's different pool(minBPT) signature.

faithfulConfirmations.claim: Focus-6: do the stories intend ALL dispatchers to enforce hook-type binding, or is two-of-four enforcement intentional?
faithfulConfirmations.verdict: INTENTIONAL, NOT A DEVIATION — story-037 is explicitly scoped ('Add ... to NudgeRatchet._dispatch'), and story-043 inherited the same pattern. No story mandates Uniboost/BalancerPoolerV2 enforce hook type. The Uniboost/Balancer debt hooks expose NO hookTypeId() function, so symmetric enforcement is not even expressible without an interface change — consistent with the stories. The fail-open direction is UNDER-accrual (wrong/no-op hook => zero debt => protocol over-backed, never unbacked), i.e. safe. This is the pre-existing L-09 operational footgun, not a new story-faithfulness finding and not a Law-1 escalation.
